title: data-objectstack: createErrorFromResponse stamps status 500 on an error that got no answer, so a dropped connection reads as an answered server error
body:
domain:ui#2 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jRFuJz9QBZqPVHYVhJ

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding, class a (read and measured), from #29728 (PR #29883). Filed by `domain:ui#2`. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

**Business reason.** When a request gets no answer at all (the connection dropped, the host is unreachable), any caller that reads the adapter's error believes the server answered with a 500. A screen that follows #29704's rule then shows the browser's "Failed to fetch" as if it were the server's own sentence, when it should say "check your connection".

## What happens (measured on `main` `99c06965`, real `ObjectStackAdapter` + fake fetch)

- `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/errors.ts` `createErrorFromResponse`: `const status = response?.status || response?.statusCode || 500`. A `TypeError` from `fetch` has no status, so it becomes an `ObjectStackError` with code `UNKNOWN_ERROR` and `statusCode` 500.
- The function also replaces the server's ADR-0112 code with the adapter's own taxonomy (a 503 becomes `ConnectionError` / `CONNECTION_ERROR`, a 500 becomes `UNKNOWN_ERROR`).
- In-tree there is one caller, `ObjectStackAdapter.getObjectSchema`'s non-404 catch. It is read at 58 call sites in 43 files under `ui/`. The function is also exported from `@object-ui/data-objectstack`.
- #29728 (PR #29883) works around this for the by-name route read only: the wrapper now keeps the transport error as `details.originalError`, and `MetadataProvider` reads that cause. Every other `getObjectSchema` caller that classifies the wrapper still reads a network drop as an answered 500.

## Wanted

A status-less error is not answered as 500. One way is to keep `statusCode` undefined, or to give the error a no-answer class such as `ConnectionError` with no status. `classifyLoadError` / `answeredLoadFailure` would then read it as `network` everywhere. Decide whether the wrapper should also carry the server's own `code` beside its taxonomy code. The function is exported, so a change to what it returns may be a Clause-② question for the claim.

## Tests

- A `getObjectSchema` call whose fetch rejects with a `TypeError` produces an error that `answeredLoadFailure` returns `null` for, and `classifyLoadError` reads as `network`.
- CONTROL: an answered 503 / 500 keeps its status.
- Ablation: put the `|| 500` back, and the first test goes red.

Landing site: `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/errors.ts` and its tests. Callers only if a test shows one depends on the 500.

Dedupe: `is:issue createErrorFromResponse`, `is:issue "Failed to fetch" 500 network` (none open).

Links back: #29728, #29704.
